statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-57108 (GHSA-rp2p-6cmp-jxj9) is a .NET denial of service issue on Linux and macOS: a specially crafted X.509 certificate can crash the runtime's native cryptography layer (CryptoNative_GetX509NameInfo) while it is parsed. Microsoft lists the .NET 10.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, as affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.9 and fixed in 10.0.10 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rp2p-6cmp-jxj9, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/408, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.10/10.0.10.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: every build ships the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework, which holds the System.Security.Cryptography assemblies and the native OpenSSL shim library they call, at its own .NET version, in dotnet10-runtime and in the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap. In dotnet10-runtime the shim library (libSystem.Security.Cryptography.Native.OpenSsl.so, which exports CryptoNative_GetX509NameInfo) carries version 10.0.2 to 10.0.9 in the first eight builds and 10.0.10 or later from 10.0.10-r0 on, on both architectures. The range ends at 10.0.10-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
